resources.string: Desqueezes photos taken through a Moment anamorphic lens (1.33x or 1.55x) with your regular camera app, so you keep its full HDR+ / Night Sight processing. The corrected copy keeps all of the photo\'s metadata (date, location, camera details) and lands next to the original, where Google Photos backs it up.

1. Shoot with the anamorphic lens in your normal camera app. The photo looks squeezed.
2. Open it in Google Photos (or any gallery) and tap Share.
3. Pick Stretch to desqueeze it, or Unstretch to undo a stretch.

Nothing else to do: the app has no camera and no internet access.
1.33x turns 4:3 photos into 16:9. Pick 1.55x for Moment\'s 1.55x anamorphic lens.

Leave this off if landscape photos come out too narrow (the lens as Moment ships it, flares horizontal in landscape). Turn it on if portrait photos come out too narrow instead: your lens has been turned 90° with the hex tool.
After saving the processed copy, move the original to the trash. Android asks you to confirm, and you can restore it from the trash for 30 days.
Granted. The app can find the original photo to keep its location and to replace it.
Not granted. Without it the app can still stretch photos, but it may not be able to replace the original or keep location data.
Free and open source (MIT). Not affiliated with Moment. Source code, help and updates: https://github.com/VladislavEkimtcov/AndroidMomentAnamorphicLens
